niche: a provincial housing ministry setting the five-year housing target for a suburban city's transit-oriented areas, forecasting the net new homes that building permits will add each year 2027 to 2031 on the lots the 2027 order upzones around four rapid transit stations to 3.0, 4.0 and 5.0 FAR, where concrete towers do not pay
stakeholder_role: senior analyst in the provincial housing ministry's housing targets branch, preparing the city's 2027 to 2031 target order

spine.entity: one folio (a legal lot, or a strata lot in a strata plan) on one year's assessment roll
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a BC Assessment roll extract)

world.geography: Canada, British Columbia (a fictional suburban city on a fictional rapid transit line)
world.org_type: provincial housing ministry (housing targets branch) setting a municipal housing target order

driver: The forward yield of a raised allowance is each unit's chance of being rebuilt, nil until the best-paying option the allowance permits is worth more than what stands there and then the steady rate units of its kind have shown once rebuilding paid, times that option's output, which past a cost step in the construction method stays below the allowance; the allowance's capacity at a past change's take-up, a model on the visible attributes, or the option the allowance names all miss it.
driver_concrete: Under the 2027 transit-area order a lot is rebuilt only once the building that pays best, priced from the market study's values and the cost guide's costs, is worth more than the assessed value of what stands on it, and then at the rate lots of its kind (houses, commercial sites, rental apartments) have shown since 2014 once rebuilding paid; at the four suburban stations concrete towers never pay, so the 4.0 and 5.0 FAR tiers yield the same six-storey wood frame as the 3.0 tier, and zoned capacity at the 2018 corridor rezoning's take-up overstates the yield.
stump: A strong solver takes each transit-area lot's capacity under the order (lot area times its tier's FAR, at 85 per cent net over 820 square feet a home, less the homes on it) and the share of capacity the 2018 corridor rezoning has delivered each year, and files about 2,800 net new homes a year for 2027 to 2031 against about 2,050 falling to 1,750; the step that lands it there is reading capacity as yield, when a lot is rebuilt only once the building that pays best is worth more than what stands on it, at the rate its kind of lot has shown once that held, and at these stations that building is the six-storey wood frame at 3.0 FAR, never the 4.0 and 5.0 FAR towers the order allows.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who stitches the two roll layouts, links permits to lots through the folio history and reads the order's tiers and the target methodology correctly computes zoned capacity on the transit-area lots and applies the take-up the 2018 corridor rezoning has shown, filing about 2,800 net new homes a year; only each lot's feasibility at the building that pays best, and the rate feasible lots of each kind have redeveloped, gives about 2,050 falling to 1,750.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the housing a rezoning will actually produce, which urban land economics estimates lot by lot from development feasibility (the residual land value of the best-paying permitted building against the value of the existing use) and the observed redevelopment rate of sites once feasible; with another field's nouns there is no residual land value, no construction-type cost step and no existing use for a new building to outbid.
layer1: assessment roll extracts in two layouts, a 2019 schema change renaming and splitting the value columns, with lot area in square feet for most folios and in acres for the larger ones
folios retired and new folios created when lots are consolidated or subdivided, linked only through a folio history table
strata plans carried as one folio per strata lot, each with its own assessed value
building permits keyed by civic address and one or more folio numbers, a consolidated site's permit listing every folio it spans
floor area recorded in square feet before the permit system's 2020 metric switch and in square metres after
demolished homes recorded both on the new-building permit and on a separate demolition permit for the same lot
permits cancelled, expired or superseded by a revised permit after issue
secondary suites and laneway homes permitted under their own permit types
zone codes on the roll as in force at the roll's valuation date, renamed in the 2020 bylaw consolidation
the order's schedule of lots as at its date, some folios since consolidated or renumbered

lineage.niche: a Scottish health and social care partnership forecasting how many care home residents it will be paying for at each quarter end of 2027-28, when the second stage of a rise in the upper capital limit on 5 April 2027 brings every self-funding resident's savings to the limit sooner, a step the history saw once, smaller, on 6 April 2026
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the inflow a pool sends over a forward window that holds an announced step in the threshold ending each member's duration clock: the hazard fitted on the history carries none of it, its size is read from the one smaller step the history holds as that day's excess entries over an ordinary week in units of clock time, scaled by the ratio of the steps, and it enters the forecast as a jump in every member's clock that brings in those it carries past the threshold on the day and moves the rest on.
lineage.driver_concrete: Self-funding care home residents come onto council funding when their capital reaches the upper limit; the limit, frozen since 2019, rose by 5,000 pounds on 6 April 2026 and rises by 7,000 on 5 April 2027, so the conversion hazard by months since admission fitted on 2021 to 2026 misses the 2027 step; 6 April 2026 brought 8 conversions against 1.6 in an ordinary week (4.8 weeks of drawdown), so 5 April 2027 is 6.7 weeks, applied as a jump in every self-funder's clock on top of the 4.8 weeks the 2026 pool already carries.
lineage.stump: A strong solver who builds the conversion hazard by months since admission from the payment lines, with deaths and discharges competing, and projects today's 581 self-funders through it files 770, 780, 790 and 790 (768.7, 778.0, 787.2 and 794.1) against 790, 800, 810 and 810; the step that lands it there is projecting the 2021 to 2026 hazard through 5 April 2027, when the upper capital limit rises by 7,000 pounds and every self-funder's savings reach it about 6.7 weeks sooner, a step the history saw once, at 5,000 pounds on 6 April 2026 (8 conversions that day against 1.6 in an ordinary week).
lineage.answer: Budget for 790, 800, 810 and 810 council-funded long-stay care home residents on 30 June, 30 September and 31 December 2027 and 31 March 2028.

lineage.niche: the same world and call, round 1's decisive step: the self-funding pool's conversion by months since admission
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the inflow that a pool held outside the decision's own register will send into it over the forward year, generated by a conversion hazard that is near zero for a member's first months and peaks a year or more after entry; because a recent surge filled the pool with members not yet in their conversion window, the inflow counted in past years, or a pooled per-member rate, understates it, and only the hazard by time since entry applied to each member's own entry date sizes it.
lineage.driver_concrete: Self-funding care home residents become council-funded when their savings fall to the threshold, which almost never happens in the first months and mostly happens one to three years after admission; two new private homes filled with self-funders in 2025-26, so the partnership's transfer counts of past years and its transfers per self-funder both understate 2027-28, and only conversion by months since admission, applied to each self-funder's admission date, sizes the council-funded caseload.
lineage.stump: A competent solver projects the council-funded caseload from the placements register, current residents by survival plus direct admissions and conversions from self-funding at their 2024 to 2026 run rate, and files about 740 residents at 31 March 2028 (740.3, and 740 at every quarter end of 2027-28) against 760 rising to 790; the step that lands it there is treating conversions as a steady route when they are generated by the self-funding pool by months since admission, and that pool, 599 against 415 at the end of 2024, is now mostly 2025-26 admissions (505 of the 599 admitted from 1 January 2025) about to enter the one to three years in which savings run down to the upper capital limit.
lineage.answer: Budget for 760, 770, 780 and 790 council-funded long-stay care home residents on 30 June, 30 September and 31 December 2027 and 31 March 2028.
lineage.fate: shipped 2026-10-12, judged weak by the 10/10 audit of 2026-10-14: the decisive step (the conversion hazard by months since admission) was reachable from the surface and the determinism judge built it unprompted (760.0, 771.0, 781.2 and 790.3 against 760, 770, 780 and 790); round 2 makes it the default path and moves the decisive step to the 2027 capital-limit step

lineage.niche: a border county's criminal justice planning office projecting how many of next fiscal year's jail releases will be followed by a return within three years, when some releases are deported or die before they can return, to size a state-funded reentry navigator grant by supervision district
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the probability that a released unit has an event within a fixed horizon when some units leave through exits that are not censoring and most units are not yet followed to the horizon: the share observed so far understates it, the survival estimate that censors those exits overstates it most where they concentrate, treating the exit that can be reversed as final understates it, and only following every unit to the data cut sizes the allocation.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each supervision district's probability that a release is booked into the jail again within 36 months is estimated from releases since the bail reform, none followed for the full 36 months, while transfers on an immigration detainer end mostly in removal, some removed people come back and are booked again, and some releasees die; the share booked again so far understates it, Kaplan-Meier with removals and deaths censored overstates it most in the border district, a cumulative incidence that ends follow-up at removal drops the returns after people come back, and following every release to the data cut, times next year's projected releases, sets the navigators by district.
lineage.stump: A competent solver estimates each district's 36-month return probability by Kaplan-Meier from post-reform releases, censoring removals and deaths along with the data cut, and applies for too many navigators with the border district over-allocated; the step that lands it there is treating deportation and death as loss to follow-up, when a removed person who comes back is booked into the same jail and a dead releasee can no longer return.
lineage.answer: We should apply for 33 reentry navigators: 8 in Puerto, 8 in Centro, 4 in Norte, 6 in Poniente, 4 in Oriente and 3 in Sur, for 7,441 projected returns from fiscal 2027 releases.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-11 at hardening loop 1 of 3: round 1 landed the call exactly (33 navigators, 7,441 projected returns, proxy 82.3) on the default construction (Kaplan-Meier with the cut as the only censoring, deaths as non-returners), which was the golden; the stump (censoring removals and deaths) sat off that path, and loop 1 found on paper no rung on it that is analytical, forced, fork-free and outside the bin (period, mix, a younger window, a forward booking change, a release pulse and visible exits all measured dead)
